findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a single use 2 oz cup stored in powdered sugar and cinnamon sugar. CORRECTED- the cup was removed and discarded. The person in charge (PIC) stated they are actively reminding employees to not use scoops without handles in ready to eat (RTE) foods. Ensure all RTE foods are handled with gloves, deli paper, or a scoop with a handle- to differentiate between the food contact and hand contact surface moving forward to prevent bare hand contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT. [P]

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
FIRST REPEAT: Inspector observed a food handler on shift with no Food Handler certificate available. All employees must have food handler who handle food must have certificates to be made available during inspections within 30 days of employment. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically. [C]

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
SECOND REPEAT: The CFM has not completed Allergen Training. Complete training and test to be made available by the next routine inspection. Certified Food Protection Managers at high risk establishments must complete Allergen Awareness training and test within 30 days of employment, to be renewed every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. [C]

findings.comment: Inspector observed unlabeled spray bottle beneath the front counter. The PIC verified that the substance was sanitizer. CORRECTED- the PIC labeled the container to display the contents. Ensure all chemicals are properly labeled to prevent food contamination.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Inspector observed white powder at the fry station to contain no label. CORRECTED- the PIC identified and labeled the food as powdered sugar. Ensure all RTE foods that may be mistaken for other foods are labeled once removed to from their original container to prevent cross contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD. [C]

findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple areas within the physical facility in need of repair or cleaning:
1) An accumulation of dust and debris on the shelf above the drive through. Clean nonfood contact surfaces at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
2) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the kitchen.
3) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the mens’ restroom.
4) Caulking between the hand washing sink and wall in the womens’ restroom.
5) Caulking along the back and right side border of the triple sink. 
Physical facilities that may not be moved for cleaning must be adhered to the wall to prevent the entry and harborage of mold. Ensure physical facilities are cleaned and repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.comment: Inspector observed liquid cheese sauce to have an ambient temperature of 125F, and was probed to have an internal temperature of 126F. CORRECTED- the liquid cheese was voluntarily discarded by the PIC. Liquid cheese was moved to used time as a control for food safety (TAC). The outside of the container was marked with a discard time 4 hours past when the bag was opened. Other options may include using a ladle for liquid cheese until the hot holding unit is serviced or replaced. Hot holding units for hot TCS items must be maintained at or above 135F.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above, except that roasts cooked to a temperature and for a time specified in 3-401.11(B) or reheated as specified in 3-403.11(E) may be held at a temperature of 54°C (130°F) or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control.
findings.comment: Inspector observed the Ortega Liquid cheese dispenser to be inadequately holding hot temperatures- see violations #21. Hot holding units must reach temperatures to hold TCS foods at or above 135F. Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to check that the unit is properly hot holding foods. Repair or replace unit.
findings.citation_text: 4-301.11 Cooling, Heating, and Holding Capacities. EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. [Pf]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple incidents of improper utensils storage:
1) Both the chopped tomatoes and onions contained single service bowls with no handles in the food.
2) The ice scoop handle was touching the ice in the drive-thru.
CORRECTED. The single service bowls in the produce were discarded, and the ice scoop was moved to its holder. Scoops with handles should be stored so that the nonfood contact surfaces (the handle, which is touched) is stored above or separate from the food to prevent bare-hand contamination. Do not reuse bowls as scoops, as there is no differentiation between the food-contact surface and the hand contact surface. Either Immediately discard bowl after use, or obtain scoops with handles for produce.
findings.citation_text: 3-304.12(A) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) Except as specified under (B) of this section, in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed a significant accumulation of burnt food debris on the interior of the quesadilla grill, and grease on the outside of the quesadilla grill. Ensure food contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris. Old food debris could serve as a source of contamination for RTE foods. Inspector will return on 10/24/25 to inspect quesadilla grill cleaning.

4-101.11(B)-(E) Characteristics. Materials that are used in the construction of UTENSILS and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to FOOD and under normal use conditions shall be: (B) Durable, CORROSION-RESISTANT, and nonabsorbent; (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness to withstand repeated WAREWASHING; (D) Finished to have a SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface; and (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. [C]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Inspector observed insect trap placed above clean dish ware (on storage rack between office and mop sink). PIC was notified to have pest control company move trap away from food-contact surfaces to prevent contamination. Insect control devices should not be located over areas where food is being prepared, or where clean equipment is being stored. [C]
findings.citation_text: 6-202.13 Insect Control Devices, Design and Installation. (A) Insect control devices that are used to electrocute or stun flying insects shall be designed to retain the insect within the device. (B) Insect control devices shall be installed so that: (1) The devices are not located over a FOOD preparation area; and (2) Dead insects and insect fragments are prevented from being impelled onto or falling on exposed FOOD; clean EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, and LINENS; and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice bucket faced upwards towards the ceiling- where the food contact surface can be exposed to contaminants.  CORRECTED- Education was provided to the PIC regarding potential contamination of food contact surfaces. Ice bucket was inverted. Food contact surfaces should be stored where they are not exposed to contamination. [C]
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination.

findings.citation_text: 3-501.18  A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A). [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Ice accumulation observed on the floor and ceiling of the walk in cooler. Remove ice and repair as needed to prevent the accumulation of ice in the walk-in freezer.
2) Chipped trim tiles observed near the mop sink and behind the front service counter. Repair trim so that corners are smooth and easily cleanable.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.citation_text:
3-301.11 1) Ice scoop was buried in the ice inside the ice machine bin. Ice in contact with handle was removed and used to chill pans of food on cold line. 
2) Ice scoop in the bin at drive thru was observed with the handle down touching ice. Scoop was repositioned to allow for proper storage with handle up out of ice. Ensure proper storage in scoop holder or in ice with handle up out of ice.
Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in  (D) and (E) of this section, food employees may not contact exposed, ready-to-eat food with their bare hands and shall use suitable utensils such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing equipment.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Spray bottle and sani-bucket at front service counter were observed at or below 100ppm quat. Solutions were refreshed and provided at 200pm for all sani-buckets and 3 part sink. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration, and maintain solutions at 200-400ppm as directed by product label. Ensure spray bottles of sanitizer are refreshed as needed prior to concentration becoming weak and ineffective.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) 1) In-use pouches of sour cream and guacamole had surface temperatures at 55F-56F. Dispensed portions were probed at 53F-54F. Products are typically held at ambient temperature on make line taco racks during service. Time control policy was established for working supplies of sour cream and guacamole. 
2) Lettuce on cold line ice bath as observed with internal temperatures of 41F-50F depending on where temperature was checked. Ice bath was refreshed to surround the pan on all sides and help maintain product at colder temperature. Lettuce in question would be used or discarded by the end of dinner service.
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.18 Rice portions in walk-in cooler had prep date or 12/11. Portions should have been used or discarded by close of business on 12/17. Date marking was discussed, and rice was discarded. Educational handout on date marking was provided. 
A food specified in  3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in  3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or package that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in  3501.17(A).

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle at front counter was unlabeled as to the contents. Bottle had sanitizer that was not at proper concentration. Solution was discarded. Ensure all spray bottles are properly labeled as to the contents.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site (bleach solution, etc.) shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. At least one employee that has worked at the facility for longer than 30 days has an expired food handler certification. Ensure re-certification occurs before next routine inspection. Maintain copies of food handler certifications at the facility.
All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed touching the manual faucet with their hands to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Ensure proper handwashing between tasks.
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 1) Manager was observed banging bagged ice on the floor to break apart frozen chunks of ice prior to placing ice on the cold line. Bag was visibly soiled and had a tear in one side. Manager was allowed to use ice as it was only coming in contact with the outer surfaces of containers and not used for consumption. However, the soiled outer surface of the bag came in contact with the taco rack where shells sit during prep while pouring ice in the cold holding well. Manager noted the taco rack in question is rarely used and was advised on the concerns for cross contamination. Taco rack was removed to be cleaned and sanitized. Better option of breaking ice on a counter surface was discussed. 
2) Cinnamon sugar mix was in an uncovered container on the bottom shelf of the stainless steel table next to the fryers. Grease buildup was observed on the underneath surface of the table directly above the uncovered container. Covering product to avoid potential dripping of grease from soiled surface was discussed, and a lid was provided. 
Food shall only contact surfaces of equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified under Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of the 2017 FDA Food Code; single-service/single-use articles, or linens such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3-304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11 Can opener blade was soiled with stuck on food debris and metal shavings around the blade. Stuck on buildup also observed on the upper surfaces on both sides of the blade. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during inspection.
Food contact surfaces shall be clean to sight and touch. Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils between uses.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 (C) & (D) Two tamales were observed in the steamer on the make line. Surface and internal temperatures were at 120F-123F. Employee working on the make line confirmed the tamales were in the steamer since this morning. Tamales were discarded in the trash during inspection. Proper reheating of commercially processed, ready to eat (RTE), time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods was discussed. Ensure proper heating of all foods. **See general comments for additional information**
RTE TCS food that has been commercially processed and packaged in a food processing plant that is inspected by the regulatory authority that has jurisdiction over the plant, shall be heated to a temperature of at least 135F when being reheated for hot holding. 
Reheating for hot holding as specified under  (A) - (C) of this section shall be done rapidly and the time the food is between 41F and the temperatures specified under  (A) - (C) of this section may not exceed 2 hours.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Pouch of sour cream was observed out on the make line. Dispensed portion of sour cream was observed at 59F. Manager noted the sour cream was supposed to be in a container specified for cold holding of product on the cold line. Ensure proper cold holding of sour cream if the intent is to keep product cold. Otherwise, management needs to establish and adhere to a time control policy. Employee on make line noted the product was in use for ~1hr. Sour cream was to be used or discarded within the next 3hrs. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (B) Pan of refried beans in the walk-in cooler was observed without a date mark. Beans were made two days prior and were dated during inspection. Ensure proper date marking of prepared foods.
A Refrigerated, ready to eat, TCS food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41F/below for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

findings.citation_text:

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 (A)(2) Pouches of whipped topping on a cart near the fryers had surface temperatures of 55F-53F. A pouch of sour cream on the same cart had surface temperatures of 50F-44F. One of the pouches of whipped topping had an internal temperature of 51F-61F and was discarded. PIC noted the products were out for ~20 minutes or so and were in the process of being stocked when inspector arrived. Remaining portions were buried in ice on the make line and were to be used or discarded within the next 4hrs or less. 
Ensure foods that require cold holding are properly stocked within ice on make line upon removal from cold holding. If interruption occurs, place items back in the reach-in or walk-in cooler until proper attention can be provided for prep/stocking of the make line. Leave foods in coolers until they are needed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11 PIC was in the process of reheating refried beans in the microwave upon arrival of inspector. Temperature was checked with a food thermometer, but the thermometer was positioned on the outer edge of the container. PIC was advised on checking the internal temperature in the center of the product. PIC was then observed moving the food thermometer around in the product from the side into the middle and back to the side of the container. Beans were stirred and placed back in the microwave for additional heating. Refried beans were placed in steam table for hot holding prior to internal temperature reaching 165F/above throughout. Inspector took the internal temperature of refried beans after being placed in the steam table and observed pockets of product below 165F with temperatures in the 140F-150F range. Upon stirring the internal temperature in the middle was observed between 158F-160F. PIC verified the temperature was checked by moving the thermometer around as previously observed.  Beans were placed back in the microwave to finish properly reheating before hot holding for service. PIC stated final reheat temperature was at least 180F prior to placing back in the steam table for hot holding. Proper reheating prior to hot holding was discussed. Ensure all foods are reheated to 165F/above throughout and internal temperature is checked in the thermal center (thickest part of food/middle of the product) prior to placing in the steam table for hot holding. The steam table is intended for hot holding after foods are properly reheated. 
TCS food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the food reach a temperature of at least 165F for 15 seconds and done rapidly to the time the food is between 41F and 165F may not exceed 2 hrs.

findings.title: Gloves used properly
findings.citation_text:

Ensure gloves are changed after touching general surfaces such as boxes and after adjusting glasses, clothing, and hats/hairnets. 
Single use gloves shall be used for only one task, used for no other purpose, and discarded when damaged or soiled, or when interruptions occur in the operation.

Vegetable chopper was not used during morning prep, so food debris was left after ware washing the previous business day. Dicing plate was placed at 3 part sink for additional ware washing. Manager was advised to speak with staff about precleaning and repeating the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.citation_text:
2-301.12 Employee was observed touching the manual faucet with her hands to shut off the water prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed. Hands were properly washed prior to continuing on to the next task. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Portion of sour cream in use at the make line had surface temperatures of 51F-46F. Dispensed sour cream was observed with an internal temperature of 52F. Product was placed in the ice bath on the make line around 3pm. Remaining portion of sour cream in question would be used or discarded before 7pm. Options for cold holding, including adding ice to the pan holding product, were discussed. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.citation_text:
4-202.11 Container with diced tomatoes in the two door cooler was observed to be damaged. A rather significant crack was present along one side. Tomatoes were transferred to another container, and the damaged container was discarded. 
Food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable/free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, inclusions, pits, and similar imperfections.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-603.12 Vegetable dicer was observed in the storage area with stuck on food debris. Chopper was cleaned and sanitized after use today. Chopper was removed for additional cleaning. Manager was advised to speak with staff about precleaning and repeating the steps of ware washing as many times as necessary to ensure removal of soil from all surfaces.
If necessary for effective cleaning, utensils and equipment shall be preflushed, presoaked, or scrubbed with abrasives.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Leak was observed at the plumbing under the kitchen handsink. A pan was placed under the sink to catch dripping water. Empty the pan daily/as needed, and keep the pan clean until repairs are done.
A plumbing system shall be maintained in good repair.
